findings.description: AuditLog class wraps write() with 8 methods that are each 1–2 lines; the class interface nearly matches its implementation complexity.
dispatchReminder and dispatchCancellation are thin wrappers around sendTemplate that add no logic, creating unnecessary indirection.

Validation rules split across HTTP handlers and service layer: paging validates in both middleware and service; trip/driver inputs validate in both handlers and services; changes to validation require touching multiple modules.
Monolithic Settings interface; eleven modules independently import and fetch their 1–2 needed fields via settings(), scattering setting dependencies across the codebase.

The loan status machine is split across multiple files—type definition in shared, states/transitions/terminals/labels each in separate status files—requiring reads across 4+ files to understand what transitions are valid.
Entity-to-row serialization is duplicated identically in create, transition, and cancel methods, amplifying the cost of any Loan schema change.
Audit logging directly triggers reminder scheduling on cancellation, embedding a workflow side-effect in the audit module and hiding the connection from call sites.

Audit events are defined as hard-coded methods on AuditLog; adding a new audit event requires changes across multiple service files, and audit calls are inconsistently applied (reminders.ts does not call the audit.reminderSent method).
The nextNumber() function mutates module-level state (lastNumber) as a hidden side effect, rendering code untestable without state resets and making tests order-dependent and non-reentrant.

Settings are accessed globally from 11 modules instead of injected; changing how settings are loaded or propagated requires updates throughout the codebase and blocks testing with alternative configurations.
Activity status checking is duplicated: isActiveDriver() and stillActive() implement the same concept with different grace periods, forcing maintenance in two places and risking logic skew.
Paging validation logic is duplicated with different error strategies (fail-fast in middleware, collect-errors in validation module), applied inconsistently and validated twice in some flows.

Weekend-skipping date arithmetic (nextPaymentDue, payBy, paymentDeadline) is duplicated with subtle implementation variations; a business rule change to day-skipping logic requires coordinated edits across payment, invoicing, and reminder domains.

Config class with 12 getters and 3 setters is just a property accessor wrapper; its interface is nearly as complex as the Settings object it wraps, forcing bloated coupling everywhere config() is called.
Invoice and order ID generation use module-level mutable counters (lastNumber, sequence) that cannot be controlled or reset between tests, making ID generation fragile and non-deterministic.
Audit recording is scattered: each service manually calls record() with distinct action types; a change to audit structure or validation requires coordinated edits across all recording sites.
reminderVars() is domain-specific (reminder and order knowledge) but exported from the generic templates module, coupling template abstraction to reminder domain concerns.
Pagination validation logic is duplicated: identical checks for offset≥0, limit>0, and clamping appear in both paging() and validatePaging(), forcing changes to be made in two places.

PatientProfile wrapper has 13 methods but adds no logic—it is a 1:1 field mapping with higher interface complexity than the Patient entity it wraps; used only to call getters (getId, getName, etc.) in handlers and once via displayName() helper.

Pricing is a core domain concept scattered across calculation, bill building, rendering, and HTTP display layers; understanding or modifying pricing behavior requires bouncing between these modules across different architectural layers.

Module-level pendingFollowUps Set creates implicit global mutable state; scheduleFollowUp() and pending() rely on hidden side effects, making concurrent behavior unsafe and testing require global cleanup.
Settings loaded as a global singleton; every consumer module must know to call settings() and tests require resetSettingsForTests() to isolate.
Audit recording via record() calls scattered through service methods, mixing concerns; deepening would extract audit as a cross-cutting concern (events or decorator).
Module-level sequence counters for ID and invoice number generation prevent test isolation and parallel execution; deepening would inject a sequence provider.
Both audit and mailer maintain an in-memory array and a pluggable sink interface, splitting test reset concerns; deepening would consolidate to one pattern.
Email and phone normalization enforced only in service layer, not at store boundary; direct store.save() bypasses invariants.

Driver activity rules are implemented three different ways with different grace periods (7 days in service, 1 day in handler, 0 days in scheduler), risking inconsistent behavior and bugs when rules change.
AuditLog class exposes eight thin wrapper methods (tripCreated, tripStatusChanged, reminderSent, etc.), making its interface nearly as complex as the private write() implementation it delegates to.
ID generation for manifests and trips relies on module-level mutable counters that are neither testable in isolation nor persisted, limiting scalability and observability.

Contact information (normalization, display, phone/email parsing) scattered across four single-function modules forces service to import from multiple files; consolidating behind one interface would reduce cognitive load and make contact logic changes atomic.

Pricing imports describeLine from builder while builder imports pricing calculations, creating a cycle that couples concerns; moving procedure formatting to pricing module would break the dependency and improve testability.

Formatting amounts as currency happens three times with different rounding approaches (round, truncate, raw): consolidating behind a single interface would prevent inconsistent display across features.
Template system uses string placeholders with hardcoded variables provided only at one call site, making it impossible to validate completeness or test templates independently of their consumers.
Every module calls settings() directly as a global singleton, creating implicit dependencies that prevent injection-based testing and obscure which modules depend on which configuration values.

PatientProfile wraps Patient with 12 getter/setter methods for 7 fields but adds no behavior; used inconsistently alongside direct field access, suggesting the wrapper provides indirection without encapsulation.
Export module conditionally delegates to renderer functions without adding behavior, forcing readers to trace through three files to understand bill rendering.
Calling record() with action 'cancelled' silently triggers scheduleFollowUp(), hiding side effects from callers and creating invisible coupling between audit and reminders domains.

Loan status state machine split across four shallow files (1–7 lines each) forces understanding of status behavior to bounce between many modules; consolidating into a single LoanStatus module would reduce fragmentation.
sendTemplate() records to audit as a hidden side effect with hardcoded action and template-specific variable lookup (vars.id), coupling mailer to audit and making behavior invisible to callers.

Global pendingFollowUps Set mutated externally by scheduleFollowUp() and read by ReminderJob.pending() makes state difficult to test and reason about; injecting or explicitly returning the queue would improve testability.

Multiple modules maintain unresettable module-level state (counters for IDs and request numbers, sets and arrays for tracking), making their interfaces hard to test and preventing test isolation: calls to nextNumber(), newId(), requestId() return non-deterministic values; scheduleFollowUp() populates persistent state; recent(), byEntity(), outbox() query stale accumulated data across test runs.

The nextNumber() function increments a module-level counter as a side effect, making buildManifest() non-idempotent and untestable without managing global state; extracting numbering to a persistent store or injectable service would make manifest generation pure and testable.

Driver registration validation is split between HTTP handler (type checking) and service layer (normalization, uniqueness detection), unlike trip creation which centralizes validation; centralizing in a driver validation module would clarify where new rules belong.

Each module directly calls settings() for its own configuration needs; adding a setting or changing configuration logic requires coordinating changes across ten files instead of managing all setup in one place.

The nextNumber() function silently mutates a global lastNumber counter, making manifest numbers non-deterministic across test runs; passing the counter or generating from timestamps would expose state explicitly.

The newId() function silently mutates a global sequence counter, making trip IDs non-deterministic across test runs; threading the sequence or using content-addressed IDs would expose state explicitly.

Service methods call record() as a hidden side effect, leaving audit logic out of the interface and making it impossible to test services without side effects; capturing audit as an explicit return or callback would expose the concern.

Good dependency injection abstractions (AuditSink, MailTransport) are undermined by exposing in-memory implementation details as public methods (recent(), outbox()), coupling tests to internals.
Module-level pendingFollowUps state modified by external function and class methods leaks across implicit boundaries, making state flow opaque and testing awkward.

Payment due date calculation is implemented three times with different approaches (UTC vs local time, different weekend-handling logic); consolidating into one shared implementation would prevent inconsistency and ease maintenance.
Audit recording spans audit sink management and independent record() calls in services; extracting a shared audit abstraction would reduce scattering and ease future changes to audit behavior.
LoanGateway merely delegates every method to LoanStore without adding behavior; removing it and having LoanService use LoanStore directly eliminates unnecessary indirection.

Sequential document number generation is split across four single-function modules and composed in builder.ts; consolidating into a single NoticeNumberGenerator service would eliminate global mutable state and reduce cognitive load.

MemberStore returns raw QueryResult, forcing every caller to check rowCount and call fromRow(); LoanStore's pattern (returning domain type, throwing NotFoundError) proves a better abstraction that hides implementation details.
Bill generation, rendering, and export are split across three modules with orchestration in HTTP; understanding bill behavior requires reading all.

Amount formatting logic is duplicated with inconsistent rounding strategies (formatAmount rounds, displayAmount truncates, money does neither); changing decimal or currency rules requires updates in three places.
Settings singleton pattern leaks throughout the codebase via global function calls; testing becomes harder and dependencies remain hidden.
Pagination validation rules are duplicated in validatePaging and paging; changing constraints risks inconsistency between service and HTTP layers.
PatientProfile wraps Patient with getters and setters for each field but adds no behavior; its interface is nearly as complex as the underlying record.
Driver availability/activity status is implemented three different ways across files, forcing bouncing between files to understand or modify the business rule.
Settings are accessed globally throughout the codebase rather than injected, making it expensive to test with different configurations and impossible to isolate instances.
Services save state and log audit events as separate, non-atomic operations, risking data/audit inconsistency if failure occurs between them despite transaction support existing.
Manifest numbering relies on module-level mutable counter that resets at startup, creating risk of duplicate invoice numbers across restarts and race conditions under concurrency.

pricing.ts imports describeLine from bill/builder to format procedure lines, while builder.ts imports priceOf and pricedLines from pricing.ts, creating a circular dependency; moving describeLine to pricing breaks the cycle and co-locates line description logic with pricing calculations.
